nxs_ci_run.cause: The readiness probe required hostname-verified TLS even though this negative test deliberately provisions a resolver certificate for a different IP identity.

changes: Normal resolver readiness still requires Uvicorn started plus CA- and hostname-verified TLS/HTTP and a fail-closed 403 route response.

The deliberate resolver hostname-mismatch negative test uses an explicit readiness mode that disables hostname matching only for the readiness probe while retaining CA-chain verification, TLS listener/HTTP route proof, and the original SIP identity failure.
Unit coverage distinguishes verified identity, hostname mismatch, untrusted CA, and bounded server-start watchdog behavior.
The prior 10 second consume_committed harness timeout is reverted to the original 5 seconds because no evidence justified increasing it.

historical_stream_arm64.result: PASS in final focused verification; intermittent historical failure remains under investigation

remaining_findings: Resolver/Uvicorn readiness gap is real but is not proven to be the sole cause of historical SIP flakes.
Kamailio nxs_edge_ready is a process-init marker rather than end-to-end functional readiness.
A traced successful route showed /internal/sip/inbound=200 and /internal/sip/issue=200 well inside the five-second issue window, followed by rapid target arrival.
Other traced failures occurred at later SIP dialogue observations, so a single startup cause remains unproven.
